- No subnational variation.

But: enforced sodomy law with documented enforcement, strict public morality enforcement, official discrimination persisting, arrest of a person for feminine appearance in 2017 (pre-striking), film/content censorship, no recourse/no civil society, no legal recognition, dress-code policing continuing post-2022 (documented as "did not end the dress-code policing").

Post-2022 official discrimination persists. No remedy infrastructure, no NGO, blocked advocacy.

Given: criminalisation of same-sex conduct is secondary for trans visitors, but here the dossier explicitly says "A trans visitor in what would be locally classed as a same-sex relationship, or read as such under birth-sex status, faces this exposure regardless of the 2022 ruling" — that's a documented traveler-facing exposure. And it's enforced.

So I'd place this around 0.30-0.40. It's not tier-1 universal facility exclusion. But it has: enforced criminal statute reaching the traveler (imprisonment up to 7 years), continuing police dress-code policing, official discrimination, no recourse, no civil society, censorship, HIV deportation of foreigners.

Let me settle: 0.34-0.36. I'll go with 0.35.
